findings.title: The bench's shared-growth measure counts the CUDA context's own shared allocation
findings.what: Growth is the largest sample less the first. The first sample can land before the process's CUDA context has made its own shared allocation (about 64 MiB here: a sample of 4 MB, then 67 MB), so an overrun that never spills reads as a rise of up to 64 MiB, the same size as the control's spill here. Judging an overrun by whether it rises above the plateau of a run inside the cap, sampled in the same step, would separate the two, and the report could keep the samples. Changing how 'does not rise' is judged reinterprets the plan's rule, so it is for the owner to decide.
